sections.h2: Domestic and commercial, side by side
sections.html: Most insurance sites focus on either households or businesses. Real life mixes them: you might own a home, let out a flat, run a business from the spare room and drive a van for work. DomCom Insure covers both sides, so you can see where a home policy stops and business cover needs to start, and avoid gaps (or paying twice).

• Plain English first. We explain what policies do, what they usually exclude and what to check, without jargon. Our glossary decodes the rest.
  • Region by region. Rules differ across the UK, US and EU; we say which applies. See insurance in the USA and insurance in Europe.
  • Facts, not hype. We don’t invent prices, savings or star ratings. Where something changes, we date it.
  • Not advice. Our guides are general information. For complex or high-value cover, talk to a regulated broker or adviser.

DomCom Insure is free to use. Some links to insurers, brokers and comparison services may be affiliate links, which means we may earn a commission if you buy, at no extra cost to you. It never changes what we say about cover. Read how the Shmor.ai network makes money.

faqs.q: Is DomCom Insure an insurer or a broker?
faqs.a: Neither. We publish independent guides and point you to regulated insurers, brokers and comparison services. Always check a provider’s authorisation before buying.

faqs.q: What’s the difference between domestic and commercial insurance?
faqs.a: Domestic (personal lines) insurance protects individuals and households: home, contents, car, travel and life. Commercial insurance protects businesses: liability, employees, premises, professional work, vehicles and data.

In most places, motor insurance for vehicles on the road, and employers’ liability or workers’ comp once you employ staff. Lenders, landlords and clients add requirements such as buildings cover or public liability. See the table above or try the cover checker.
